name: Uzbek Khanate of Abul-Khayr
alt: Eastern wing of the Ulus of Jochi

predecessors.name: Golden Horde
predecessors.text: the independent eastern wing of the former Ulus of Jochi, around Tyumen and the Tura

successors.name: Kazakh Khanate
successors.text: the Kazakh tribes of Kerei and Janibek, c.1465-1470

successors.name: Khanate of Sibir
successors.text: the Tura and Tobol lands, under Ibak Khan (Sibir infobox)

successors.name: Shaybanids
successors.text: the Syr Darya cities Otrar, Yasi, Arkuq and Uzgend, held by the Shaybanids c.1495

ledger.x: 1428: Abu'l-Khayr is made khan at Tyumen.
c.1440: the Kazakh steppe is Abu'l-Khayr's.
1468: Abu'l-Khayr dies and his khanate breaks up.

wars.name: Abu’l-Khayr’s Khwarezm campaigns
wars.outcome: Urganj was occupied in 1430-31 but could not be held and was abandoned in summer 1431; Uzbek armies attacked Khwarezm again in 1435-36 without lasting gain.

wars.name: Uzbek conquest of the Syr Darya
wars.outcome: From 1446 Abu'l-Khayr took lands on the Syr Darya from Timurid control and made Sighnaq his capital; in 1451 he marched with Abu Sa'id on Samarkand, where Abdullah was defeated and killed, and was paid off outside the gates.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the pages give no boundary for any phase.
